newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda says to repair airbag units.
newsitem.headline: Honda says to repair airbag units.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it would conduct a voluntary recall on some Accord models to replace the airbag electronic control unit.
Honda said it had told the Transport Ministry that it would replace the units on 2,309 Accords, mostly 1995 models.
This is not a recall under Japanese rules, a Honda spokesman said.
The cars were made at Honda's Sayama plant, northern Tokyo, and at Honda of America Manufacturing in Ohio.
On Wednesday, American Honda Motor Co Inc said it would conduct a voluntary recall on 164,139 units of the 1995 Accord models for the same defect.
The total cost of repair at home and abroad is estimated at 3.7 billion yen, the spokesman said.
No accidents have been reported but the company has received 17 complaints in the United States, he said.
American Honda said the unit may cause an unexpected deployment of airbags. In some instances the unit has deployed the airbags as a result of an impact to the suspension or underbody of the vehicle.
The company said no serious injuries have been reported because of the defect.
